o1.biggest_strength: It spots the real problem: top 5 matte shades, not the matte line overall, and puts rush production plus re-cartoning ahead of the over-budget draft.
o1.biggest_mistake: It treats the held top-5 stock as already inside the 9,100 units, so it creates a December stockout gap that should mostly be closed by re-cartoning.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Correct the held-stock math so top-5 stock rises to 13,000, update the date-by-date plan, and make the foundation/kohl shade orders less dependent on a last-minute check.

o2.biggest_strength: It gives a clean Monday-ready plan inside the ₹1.2 crore cash limit, cuts liquid/glitter/slow matte ordering, and protects the top 5 shades for wedding season.
o2.biggest_mistake: It also misreads the held matte stock as included in the 9,100 top-5 units, so the planned sellout gap and some demand-control actions are more severe than needed.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Fix the re-cartoning assumption so top-5 stock becomes 13,000, then adjust the Dec 1–9 customer and ad plan around low stock rather than a full stockout.

reason: Output 2 is easier for an ops lead to run: the order table, cash use, dates, no-order lines and Monday actions are cleaner and more coherent. Both make the same held-stock math mistake, but Output 2 is the more usable plan after that correction.
